cards.explanation: The answer is False. The LORD says He “…alone stretched out the heavens, who by Myself spread out the earth…” That means He did it all Himself, with no helpers. Friends, I need bakers to fill all my cookie boxes, so I'm impressed.

The answer is that He foils and confounds them. The LORD says He “…foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners…” (Isaiah 44:25). He also “…confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense…” Their signs and their knowledge don't get them anywhere. Me, I can't even predict when my own timer will go off, so I'll stick with the Word.

The answer is rebuilt. The LORD says the cities of Judah “…will be rebuilt, and I will restore their ruins…” Ruins are not the end of the story when He's the One talking. That's good news for anybody staring at a pile of rubble.

The answer is that He'll dry them up. The LORD says to the depths of the sea, “…I will dry up your currents…” Even the deep water takes orders from Him. Friends, I can barely get my dough to stop sticking to the counter.

The answer is My shepherd. The LORD says of Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), “My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire…” Cyrus is a king, and the LORD still calls him a shepherd. I think that's a title worth hearing.

The answer is True. The LORD says of Jerusalem, “She will be rebuilt…” and of the temple, “Let its foundation be laid.” The city and the temple are both named in the same verse. For the temple, the word He uses is foundation.

The answer is to subdue nations before him. The LORD tells Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), that He has grasped his right hand “…to subdue nations before him…” The verse goes on to say it is also to disarm kings and to open the doors before him. Nations, kings and doors are all in the picture.

The answer is the LORD Himself. The LORD says to Cyrus, “I will go before you and level the mountains; I will break down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.” Level, break down and cut through are all what He says He will do. He is the One who goes before.

The answer is know. The LORD gives Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), those hidden riches “…so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.” The treasure points to who is giving it. Knowing Him is the point.

The answer is for the sake of Jacob and Israel. The LORD says, “For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I call you by name…” Jacob and Israel are His people. The call to Cyrus is for their sake.
The answer is False. The LORD says to Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), “I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known Me.” That means Cyrus had not known Him when the title was given.

The answer is so all may know there is none but Him. The LORD says, “I will equip you for battle, though you have not known Me, so that all may know, from where the sun rises to where it sets, that there is none but Me…” He means from east to west. The whole earth is in view.

The answer is prosperity and calamity. The LORD says, “I bring prosperity and create calamity.” Calamity is a heavy word. Then He closes it out: “I, the LORD, do all these things.” Light and dark, good times and hard ones, He says it's all His.

The answer is to open up so salvation may sprout. The LORD says, “Let the earth open up that salvation may sprout and righteousness spring up with it…” The skies pour down and the ground opens. Salvation sprouts like a seed.

The answer is one clay pot among many. The LORD says, “Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker—one clay pot among many.” Then He asks if the clay asks the potter, “What are you making?” Friends, a pot arguing with the potter is a very small argument.
The answer is True. The LORD says, “Woe to him who says to his father, ‘What have you begotten?’…” He adds a second one about a mother. The text gives it as another warning right behind the clay pot.
The answer is False. The LORD says, “It is I who made the earth and created man upon it.” He did both. And He says His hands stretched out the heavens.

The answer is that he won't do it for payment or reward. The LORD says Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free, “…but not for payment or reward, says the LORD of Hosts.” Not for payment. Not for reward. Those are the two things the verse rules out.
